practice_items.prompt: A malware sample spreads from device to device over the network with no user interaction and no host file. Which category best fits?
practice_items.explain: Self-propagation over a network without user action or a host file is the defining trait of a worm.

practice_items.prompt: A user installs a free video converter that secretly opens a remote-control backdoor. Which malware type is this?
practice_items.explain: Disguising malicious functionality inside apparently legitimate software is the defining trait of a trojan.

practice_items.prompt: Select ALL statements that are TRUE about ransomware.
options: It encrypts victim files and demands payment for the decryption key
It self-replicates across the network without user action
Offline backups directly neutralize its leverage
It always permanently destroys the encrypted files
practice_items.explain: Ransomware encrypts (not destroys) files and demands payment; offline backups let victims recover without paying. Ransomware does not self-propagate like a worm.

practice_items.prompt: Which property MOST distinguishes a virus from a worm?
options: Viruses encrypt files; worms do not
Viruses require a host file and user action to spread; worms spread autonomously
Viruses target networks; worms target single devices
practice_items.explain: The core distinction is propagation mechanism: viruses need a host file and user action; worms are self-contained and spread without either.

practice_items.prompt: Name the term for the initial path by which malware enters a device (e.g., a phishing email or infected USB drive).
practice_items.explain: The infection vector is the initial entry path, common examples include phishing emails, drive-by downloads, USB drives, and unpatched software exploits.

practice_items.prompt: An analyst sees that a device's CPU is near 100% and it is sending data to hundreds of IP addresses, yet no user application is open. Which malware type does this MOST suggest?
practice_items.explain: Autonomous network scanning and self-copying, consuming CPU and bandwidth without user action, is characteristic worm behavior.

practice_items.prompt: A security analyst discovers a small adapter connected between a desktop computer's USB port and the keyboard cable. No software alerts have been triggered. What type of physical attack is this?
practice_items.explain: A hardware keylogger sits between the keyboard and USB port to log typing physically without software detection.

practice_items.prompt: Which of the following mitigations specifically address threats arising from physical theft of a laptop hard drive?
practice_items.explain: Full Disk Encryption (FDE) prevents an attacker from reading data off a stolen drive, and TPM checks boot integrity before releasing keys. OS login passwords and local firewalls can be bypassed if the hard drive is physically removed and read on a different system.

practice_items.prompt: Name the keystroke injection tool disguised as a standard USB flash drive that executes pre-programmed commands by mimicking a keyboard.
practice_items.explain: A USB Rubber Ducky is a classic physical attack tool that mimics a keyboard to run commands at high speed.

practice_items.prompt: An attacker sprays compressed air (upside down) on RAM chips immediately after a workstation is powered off, then quickly moves the modules to another machine to read their contents. What is this attack called?
practice_items.explain: A cold boot attack exploits the fact that RAM contents fade gradually rather than instantly; cooling the chips slows that decay long enough to extract recently-loaded keys or passwords.

practice_items.prompt: A server room has a keypad lock on its door, but an attacker who is already an employee with legitimate badge access removes a hard drive and reads it on a personal laptop. Which control would have stopped this?
options: A security camera in the lobby
practice_items.explain: Room-level physical locks only stop people who lack access to the room. FDE protects the data itself so that even someone who can physically remove the drive cannot read it without the decryption key.

practice_items.prompt: Name the term for a sticker or label on a device's case or port that visibly tears or changes color if removed, letting staff confirm at a glance that the device has not been opened.
practice_items.explain: Tamper-evident seals provide a low-cost, visual way to detect physical tampering after the fact, commonly used on ATMs and point-of-sale terminals.

practice_items.prompt: A smart camera is still logging in with the username/password it shipped with from the factory. What is this vulnerability called?
practice_items.explain: Default credentials are factory-set login details that were never changed by the owner; attackers scan for and exploit them automatically.

practice_items.prompt: Why is the 2016 Mirai botnet a significant example in IoT security?
options: It was the first computer virus ever discovered
It encrypted victim files and demanded a ransom
It only affected desktop computers, not IoT devices
It hijacked IoT devices via default Telnet credentials and used them to launch record-setting DDoS attacks
practice_items.explain: Mirai scanned the internet for IoT devices still using default Telnet credentials, enlisted them into a botnet, and used the combined force for massive DDoS attacks.

practice_items.prompt: Select ALL statements that are TRUE about IoT device risk.
options: A device that isn't directly internet-facing can still be reached by other devices already on the same local network
Manufacturers always issue timely firmware updates for the life of the product
UPnP can automatically open a port on a router, exposing a device without the owner realizing it
Attackers often want IoT devices as botnet nodes or network pivot points, not for the device's own data
practice_items.explain: Devices on a shared network can attack each other regardless of internet exposure; UPnP can silently expose management interfaces; attackers value IoT devices mainly for scale (botnets) and as pivot points. Many manufacturers do NOT maintain updates for the full product lifetime, devices often become end-of-life (EOL).

practice_items.prompt: Which property MOST distinguishes an EOL (end-of-life) IoT device's risk from a device with an exposed management port?
options: EOL devices no longer connect to Wi-Fi at all
EOL devices always use encrypted traffic by default
EOL devices no longer receive firmware updates, so any known vulnerability stays permanently unpatched, regardless of ports or credentials
EOL devices cannot be part of a botnet
practice_items.explain: End-of-life status means the manufacturer has stopped issuing updates, so any vulnerability discovered in the firmware is never fixed for the rest of the device's life.

practice_items.prompt: Name the term for devices connected to a network without IT's knowledge, approval, or security oversight.
practice_items.explain: Shadow IoT refers to unapproved, unmonitored devices on a network that silently expand the attack surface.

practice_items.prompt: A device's mobile app sends commands to it over the local Wi-Fi network with no encryption at all. What is the MOST direct consequence?
options: The device automatically becomes part of a botnet
The device's firmware will stop receiving updates
Anyone else on the same network segment can read or alter the traffic in transit
The manufacturer's cloud API becomes unauthenticated
practice_items.explain: Unencrypted traffic can be intercepted (read) or tampered with (altered) by anyone who can observe the same network segment.
